missing: A host with mixed IOMMU domains (some TT cards identity, the rest DMA-FQ) breaks the real-time profiler on the identity cards: Metal caches the first MMIO chip's IOMMU state (tt_cluster.cpp). Now DS41-120.

ttnn.device.IsProgramRealtimeProfilerActive() is True when ONE chip runs it; the framework's profiler.require_rt should check every mesh chip (tt/rt_profiler_check.py:profiled_chips is the model-side form).
scripts/tt-probe.sh writes its probe under tests/ttnn/unit_tests/operations/<name>/probes/, outside a step's allowed paths.

overseer.evidence: Root cause found with evidence (DS41-120): /dev/tenstorrent/7 (0000:08:00.0) and /10 (0000:43:00.0) are in 'identity' IOMMU groups, the other 30 in DMA-FQ (re-enumerated after the boot-only tt-iommu-domains.service); Metal caches chip 0's IOMMU state, UMD pins 7/10 with TT_DMA_FLAG_CONTIGUOUS -> EINVAL. Hugepage exhaustion ruled out (anonymous mmap, not hugetlb). Probe on 8x4 FABRIC_2D: RT records from 30/32 chips, missing [7, 10]. Check added (tt/rt_profiler_check.py, hooks device_params + device_model, Setting RT_PROFILER_CHECK). Partial: the fix at the cause is a root host action (`sudo systemctl restart tt-iommu-domains`; no sudo here) and a tt_metal per-chip IOMMU change outside this step's paths, so the profiler still runs on 30/32 chips until the host owner acts.
No kernel or fork limit involved; nothing padded or inflated.
